name: Center for Development and Disaster Management (CDM Nepal) Bhairahawa
description:
﻿﻿Centre for Development and Disaster Management (CDM Nepal) 

Bhairahawa, Rupandehi

Terms of Reference (TOR) for Activity 3.3.1 organizing workshop to develop Green Jobs Strategic Plan of Marchawari Rural Municipality, Rupandehi

Background:

CDM-Nepal is a leading non-governmental development and humanitarian organisation of Province 5 of Nepal. Established in 2000 in Butwal, CDM-Nepal has worked in DRM, CCA, WASH, livelihood and GBV. CDM’s programmes have historically been targeted at underprivileged women and children. CDM's vision is to make just, equitable, peaceful, prosperous and disaster-resilient society for all citizens of Nepal. Major objectives include:

Reduce: Contribute to substantially reduce disaster risk and losses in lives, livelihoods and health and the economic, physical, social, cultural and environmental assets of persons, businesses, communities and countries

IMPROVE: Improve socio-economic status of the poor, marginalized and vulnerable sections of the community by implementing risk-informed, gender-responsive and inclusive livelihood improvement, health, WASH and education programmes with a rights-based perspective

PARTNERSHIP: Partner with local governments and civil society organisations for programme design, implementation and evaluation

LEARN: Generate learning through applied research on relevant socio-economic, climate, disaster, and environmental issues, and utilise this learning for advocacy and organisational development.

GOVERNANCE – Advocate and campaign at the local, province and national levels to address the root causes of development challenges

CDM-Nepal was registered with the District Administration Office of Rupandehi in 16 May 2000 with registration number 466-057/058. It is affiliated with the Social Welfare Council of Nepal Government in 2000 with registration number 11639/057. Since its establishment, it has become a member of the NGO Federation Nepal, the National Disaster Preparedness Network (DPNet) Nepal since 2008 and a founding member of the National Network of Community Disaster and Climate Risk Management Committee (NCDMC). District Disaster Management Committee (DDMC) of Rupandehi district has selected CDM-Nepal as the current District Lead Support Agency (DLSA) of Rupandehi district. Since 2017, CDM-Nepal has been providing technical and other support to the Lumbini Provincial Government as the Province Lead Support Agency (PLSA).

Introduction about the Consultancy:

Climate Change Adoption, Promotion of Green Economy are an integral part of the capacity enhancement of CDM/KZE/MISEREOR’s Community Resilience Programme. It intends to coordinate and collaborate with local governments and other community actors such as CBOs, Users Committee, school teachers, youths, child clubs, and the environment management subcommittee, who can play a pivotal role in environment-friendly initiatives at the local government and community level. To develop them as climate champions to drive climate agenda through public awareness and capacity development is the need of the era when climate change has enormous effects on lives, and livelihoods of people impacted by climate change (PICC) and gender-based discrimination.

Nepal is one of the world’s forty-eight least developed countries and such poor socio-economic conditions make the country extremely vulnerable to the effects of climate change. According to a study conducted by the Department of Hydrology and Meteorology (DHM) on climate trend analysis (2017), the annual maximum temperature trend is increasing by 0.056°C/year and Nepal’s average yearly precipitation has declined by 1.3 mm per year over the observed period (i.e., 1971-2014). As per the German Watch Report, Nepal ranked 12th in the Global Climate Risk Index in 2019, and 10th in the period 2000-2019. A rapidly changing climate in Nepal, including in the proposed districts of Rupandehi, has led to a range of adverse impacts on the socio-economic, natural, and physical environment. The climate crisis has a devastating effect on women, youth and children’s learning, safety, and wellbeing, destroys livelihood options, education services and household food security and income, forcing youth to migrate to other countries and children to drop out of school to support their family with domestic duties or work.

In this connection, this consultancy aims to raise awareness and encourage Green Jobs/entrepreneurship and its challenges among women youths, local government officials, and elected members of Marchawari Rural Municipality in Rupandehi district, as well as key entrepreneurs involved in green business.

Objective of the Consultancy:

Specific objectives include:

  • Organize a meeting of LPAC to understand green jobs opportunities including formation of a municipal committee to take lead role for the development of Green Jobs Strategic Plan
  • Identify a list of green jobs (environment and climate-friendly enterprises) that exist in the municipality and explore the possibility of new types of green jobs that are lucrative for local entrepreneurs.
  • Carry out a value chain analysis of selected top 10 green job enterprises
  • Organize a two days’ workshop with LPAC members to collate information for the development of strategic plan and share the draft plan with municipal officials
  • Preparation and finalization of Green Jobs Strategic Plan of the Palika

For detailed ToR: Click Here

Terms of Reference (TOR) for Activity 3.1.9, Conducting a study to identify green jobs opportunities, major challenges and suggest strategies for nature-based solutions including value chain analysis in Siyari and Marchawari Rural Municipalities in Rupandehi district of Lumbini Province.

Background: 

CDM-Nepal is a leading national non-governmental development and humanitarian organization with its headquarters in Butwal, Lumbini Province, Nepal. Established in 2000 in Rupandehi, CDM-Nepal has worked in disaster risk reduction, climate action, water, sanitation and hygiene promotion, livelihoods and gender equity and social inclusion, including gender-based violence. CDM’s target beneficiaries include marginalized women, children, youth and vulnerable communities. CDM worked in Rupandehi, Nawalparasi, Kapilvastu, Arghakhachi, Gulmi, Palpa, Okhaldhunga, Doti, Dadeldhura, Baitadi, Kathmandu and Achham Districts.

CDM-Nepal was registered with the District Administration Office of Rupandehi in 16 May 2000 with registration number 466-057/058. It was affiliated with the Social Welfare Council of the Nepal Government in 2000 with registration number 11639/057. Since its establishment, it has become a member of the NGO Federation Nepal, the National Disaster Preparedness Network (DPNet) Nepal since 2008 and a founding member of the National Network of Community Disaster and Climate Risk Management Committee (NCDMC). District Disaster Management Committee (DDMC) of Rupandehi district has selected CDM-Nepal as the current District Lead Support Agency (DLSA) of Rupandehi district. Since 2017, CDM-Nepal has been providing technical and other support to the Lumbini Provincial Government as the Province Lead Support Agency (PLSA).

Introduction about the Consultancy:

Climate Change Adaptation, Promotion of Green Economy and Integrated Green Growth are an integral part of the capacity enhancement of CDM/KZE/MISEREOR’s Community Resilience Programme. It intends to coordinate and collaborate with local governments and other community actors such as CBOs, Users Committee, schoolteachers, youth centre, child club (environment management subcommittee), who can play a pivotal role in environment-friendly initiatives at local government and community levels. To develop them as climate champions to drive climate agenda through public awareness and capacity development is the need of the era when climate change has huge effects on lives, and livelihoods of people impacted by climate change (PICC) and gender-based discrimination. 

Nepal is one of the world’s forty-eight least developed countries and such poor socio-economic conditions make the country extremely vulnerable to the effects of climate change. According to a study conducted by the Department of Hydrology and Meteorology (DHM) on climate trend analysis (2017), the annual maximum temperature trend is increasing by 0.056°C/year and Nepal’s annual average precipitation has declined by 1.3 mm per year over the observed period (i.e., 1971-2014). As per the German Watch Report, Nepal ranked 12th in the Global Climate Risk Index in 2019, and 10th in the period 2000-2019. A rapidly changing climate in Nepal, including in the proposed districts (Rupandehi and Nawalparasi) has led to a range of adverse impacts on the socio-economic, natural, and physical environment. The climate crisis has a devastating effect on women, youth and children’s learning, safety, and wellbeing, destroys livelihood options, education services and household food security and income, forcing youth to migrate other countries and children to drop out of school to support their family with domestic duties or work. 

This consultancy is therefore proposed to conduct a study to identify green job opportunities, significant challenges, and suggest strategies for nature-based solutions in Siyari and Marchawari Rural Municipality of Rupandehi district.

This study aims to identify existing Green Job practices/opportunities in the area, as well as explore the prospects of new, innovative, and potential green jobs/enterprises that could enhance the local economy with reduced carbon footprints. 

Objective of the Consultancy: 

The objective of this assignment is to prepare an analytical report on Green Jobs that includes the following.

  • Identify 1) a list of green jobs /enterprises (environment and climate-friendly enterprises, locally adaptable, lucrative and access to market linkages) that exist in the area and 2) recommend potential green jobs that are climate-friendly, produce high income, and have easy market access.
  • Analyze based on a) scope of environment and climate-friendly nature, b) locally adaptable, c) lucrative and d) access to market linkages
  • Recommend existing and new green enterprises mentioning reasons for recommendation and appropriateness to boost the local economy 
  • Prepare and submit study report in Nepali that needs to be presented to the municipality authorities and CDM Nepal.
  • Prepare assignment completion report in English that includes all deliverables and submit it to CDM Nepal in time.

description:
﻿Community Rural Development Society (CRDS-Nepal)

Mahakali Municipality 5 Main Road Galphai, Khalanga Darchula Ph No. 093-420061,

TRANSBOUNDARY RIVERS OF SOUTH ASIA (TROSA: T2:3R)

Call for Application: Fellowship Grant Support for One Student

Details / requirements:

Date of Publication: 8th October, 2025

Community Rural Development Society Nepal (CRDS Nepal) is a non-profit, non-governmental organization that has been actively engaged in the social development sector since 1992. Since its establishment, CRDS Nepal has been a strong advocate for the rights and empowerment of women, children, and youth. The organization strives to promote human well-being and ensure equality for all by enhancing access to education, healthcare, justice, and a violence-free society.

In line with its vision and mission, CRDS, in collaboration with Oxfam in Nepal, has been implementing the Transboundary Rivers of South Asia (TROSA) project in Darchula District. The first phase of TROSA concluded in March 2022, while TROSA Phase II has been underway since June 2023 and will continue until March 2026.

CRDS Nepal is now seeking one student fellow under its fellowship grant program to support the following activities:

2. Research Grant Opportunity

CRDS invites three Bachelor's Degree holder (masters preferred) to apply for a youth fellowship grant of NPR 100,000 (including tax). Youth Fellow initiatives are expected to lay foundations for meaningful transformation or solution to the challenges faced by grassroots communities associated with the Mahakali Basin. It could be a range of things, starting from research, documentation of indigenous knowledge revival, on-ground actions and anything innovative of its kind addresses water governance challenges in the wider sense. These initiatives are expected to be done in partnership with the communities they serve and also bring about growth to the youth leading these initiatives and add value to their journey as leaders.

3. Priorities Area of Research

Proposals must be aligned with one of the following priorities. One student will be selected for one particular topic.

  • Transboundary Cooperation Through Shared Water Governance
  • Climate resilience livelihoods in Mahakali Basin
  • Citizen Science in Water Quality Monitoring of the Mahakali River: Scope, Practices, and Sustainability

4. Eligibility Criteria for Applicants:

The Youth Fellow Initiative for Mahakali basin is open to young water leaders aged 29 years or below residing within any of the Mahakali basin. Eligible participants can apply either as individuals or as part of a group. Proposals are welcome from independent applicants as well as those affiliated with organizations. This initiative encourages innovative ideas and collaborative efforts to address water-related challenges in the region. Women and youth from indigenous or marginalized river dependent communities are strongly encouraged to apply.

5. Application Process

Interested applicants are invited to submit their proposal and CV to the official email address of CRDS, crdsprocurement@gmail.com / crdsnepal1992@gmail.comThe submitted information will be used as the basis for the shortlisting process. Applicants are requested to select one relevant topic for their research and prepare their proposal accordingly.

6. Evaluation Process

The evaluation process will prioritize initiatives that are inclusive, intersectional, innovative, and effectively address water-related challenges within the Mahakali basin. All eligible applications will undergo a thorough review by a dedicated committee comprising experts on water issues in Mahakali basin. This committee will evaluate submissions against predefined criteria and determine grant allocation. Shortlisted candidates will proceed to the next phase, where they will receive orientation to meet the objective of their study and be invited to submit a full comprehensive proposal detailing their initiative. Final selection will be based on the strength of these proposals, and support will be provided accordingly.

7. Evaluation Criteria

I. Relevance: The proposed initiative must align with the pressing needs of the communities dependent on the Mahakali River basin for transboundary cooperation, climate resilience livelihoods, citizen science in its scope, and survival. Initiatives that are well studies/documents the power relations, vulnerabilities, rights, justice, and opportunities in the context of their river basins will be prioritized.

II. Potential Impact: The initiative/research should advocate for the equitable use of water resources, addressing social and environmental equity challenges, and fostering inclusive and resilient communities.

III. Innovation, Creativity and Capacity: Novel and effective strategies, especially for engaging women, youth, and Indigenous peoples, addressing policy gaps, participation and influencing stakeholders.

IV. Sustainability and Scalability: The initiative needs to address sustainability and beyond as the result of study/research or influencing policy and advocacy to ensure long-term impact.

8. Reporting Requirements

The YF will receive an orientation on the Mahakali basin, TROSA’s working areas, and mutual expectations. This will be followed by two follow-up meetings to track progress and provide necessary support. The final report is due by 26 January 2026.

name: Helambu Education and Livelihood Partnership (HELP)
description:
﻿﻿﻿﻿﻿﻿Recruitment for 7th cohort of Saathi Teachers

Job Description 

Background

Saathi Teachers Programme is an educational initiative under Helambu Education and Livelihood Partnership (HELP) operating under the theme of ‘Primary Must Not Be Secondary. It offers paired and paid placement for individuals seeking to teach Math or English at Basic Level in rural communities in order to help transform the educational experience of children. It is two years of supervised programme to increase literacy and numeracy skills of students, with additional focus on fostering and developing 4C (Creativity, Critical thinking, Communication, and Collaboration) skills in students. 

Saathi Teachers Programme work in partnership with the local government and the schools to assist the overall growth of the students and the school. We currently work in three Rural Municipalities- Paanchpokhari Thangpal Rural Municipality and Tripurasundari Rural Municipality in Sindhupalchowk district, and Aanbookhaireni Rural Municipality in Tanahun district. The partner municipalities pay for the large part of the Saathi Teachers’ direct stipend and the programme’s operational part is largely supported by Mondo Foundation, our UK partner organization, with contribution from Inter Hands Foundation to ensure we can sustain the programme in three municipalities. 

About HELP: 

Helambu Education and Livelihood Partnership (HELP) is a local NGO set up in 2009 intending to improve the quality of education in remote schools of Sindhupalchowk. As a grassroots local non-profit organization, we currently run five core programmes; Saathi Teachers Programme, Scholarship and Leadership Programme, School in a Bag Programme, Volunteer Programme and Livelihood Support Programme, designed and aimed to complement each other and strengthen the quality of education. For more detail on HELP’s activities. Please visit our website to know more about our programme.

'Saathi Teachers Programme is pleased to announce applications open for its 7th cohort of Saathi Teachers!'

APPLY NOW TO BECOME A SAATHI TEACHER 

We are looking to recruit 20 Saathi Teachers in the 7th cohort to work in our partner municipalities- Paanchpokhari Thangpal Rural Municipality and Tripurasundari Rural Municipality in Sindhupalchowk district, and  Aanbookhaireni Rural Municipality in Tanahun district. The cohort after selection will have to attend Saathi Teachers programme events and graduate from a few weeks long pre-service residential training taking place towards the end of this academic year, and finally start working as a Saathi Teacher from Baisakh 2083 for two years. 

Working Area: Sindhupalchowk and Tanahun

Contract term: Two years of absolute commitment 

Reports to: Teachers Development Coordinator (TDC) 

Core Duties and Responsibilities:  

  • Teach English or Mathematics from grade 1 to 5 in the placed schools. 
  • Develop and integrate 21st-century 4Cs skills (Creativity, Collaboration, Critical Thinking, Communication) into everyday classroom activities.
  • Use innovative and child-centered teaching approaches and methods to engage students and create a safe and inclusive learning environment in the classroom 
  • Prepare annual, trimester, unit and daily lesson plans for assigned subjects in line with the national/ local curriculum.
  • Prepare and utilize various teaching and learning materials to engage the students and make learning fun 
  • Plan and execute in-class and outdoor activities and events to enhance the academic and non-academic skills of the students 
  • Conduct regular classroom assessment of students and track them 
  • Maintain accurate records and portfolio of students' academic performance and report them to school stakeholders and the TDCs
  • Under direct supervision of the Principal and the SMC, work towards implementing the School Improvement Plan 
  • Communicate, consult and cooperate with other teachers and staff of the school, parents/guardians to ensure the best interest of students.
  • Reflect and evaluate one's teaching and learning strategies and methodologies align with the National Education Goals
  • Prepare and submit trimester reports, reflections, write ups and other reports to the TDC
  • Work together as a member of cluster and provide support in cluster initiatives and projects 
  • Participate and contribute to shared learning by attending quarterly trainings and mid-year trainings
  • Conduct a small-scale Community Action Project (CAP) within two years of Saathi journey to identify and address critical issues within their placed communities
  • Perform any other duties as assigned by the school Principal 

Knowledge, Skill and Attitude

  • Bachelor’s degree in relevant field (preferred) but completion of secondary school (+2) is the minimum requirement 
  • Passionate about teaching children and working in the rural community
  • Knowledge of primary subjects as per the curriculum
  • Some knowledge of child psychology, pedagogy and curriculum
  • Classroom management and behaviour management skills
  • Assessment design, evaluation and presentation skills
  • Theme-based activity-centric teaching skill
  • Exceptional organizational skills to keep on top of these tasks and complete their duties on time
  • Intellectually challenging and encouraging students
  • Good communication and social skills
  • Knowledge sharing and a passionate learning attitude
  • Patience, empathy and problem-solving attitude 
  • Ability and adaptability to live in minimum living conditions

description:
﻿Vacancy Announcement

Position: NDI Asia-Pacific Regional Specialist for Monitoring, Evaluation and Learning

Founded in 1983, the National Democratic Institute for International Affairs (NDI) is a nonprofit, nonpartisan organization working to strengthen and expand democracy worldwide. NDI works with democratic institutions in every region of the world to build political and civic organizations, safeguard elections and promote citizen participation, openness, and accountability in government. Headquarters in Washington, DsociaC, and NDI maintain offices in over 70 countries on five continents. Its diverse workforce of employees from 75 countries is united in the belief that democracies promote economic growth and development more consistently and equitably than non-democratic political systems. NDI’s office in Nepal has been operational since 1994 and has since collaborated with the Parliament, political parties, government agencies and civil society.

Position Summary: This specialist guides the implementation of NDI programming and provides technical assistance to NDI staff in the Asia-Pacific region and headquarters in the areas of program design, monitoring, evaluation and learning (DMEL). This position is based in the Nepal and reports to the Nepal Country Representative and the NDI Asia-Pacific deputy regional director.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

With direction from Asia-Pacific regional leadership and country/ program leadership:

  • Provide technical guidance and support in the coordination and execution of DMEL activities and processes;
  • Support country and program teams with program design, monitoring and evaluation plans, data collection tools and processes, ensuring sound performance monitoring and evaluation systems and protocols;
  • Participate in and support operationalizing the monitoring and evaluation of program performance against established plans and indicators through data collection and analysis methodologies, instruments, and protocols;
  • Guide the analysis, visualization, and interpretation of program performance data to support its use in decision-making, donor reporting, and collaborative learning and adaptation. Help country and program teams execute analysis and review processes to support data-driven learning, adaptation, and interventions for necessary course corrections;
  • Participate in program assessments and evaluations. Guide program and country teams on the preparation of program performance and impact evaluations and reports;
  • Support preparations for learning discussions and reflections to identify evaluation recommendations and program management improvements;
  • Support implementation of regional learning sessions for cross-regional learning between program teams on best practices and evidence;
  • Help coordinate necessary training and resources for country and program teams to build regional DMEL knowledge and capacity as well as data collection and management competencies;
  • Develop and foster effective working relationships with country and program teams, and help facilitate collaborative and inclusive processes to identify and implement regional DMEL activities, and ensure alignment with broader institutional strategies and approaches;
  • Support DMEL for program development opportunities and processes;
  • Perform other duties as required by regional leadership.

EDUCATIONAL BACKGROUND AND EXPERIENCE

  • Bachelor’s degree required, preferably in social sciences, statistics, evaluation, international development or other relevant discipline or equivalent experience.
  • A minimum of eight (8) years of experience in monitoring and evaluation, preferably in the field of democracy and governance, international development, social science, data analysis, or statistics, and with I/NGO experience.
  • Experience in the design of monitoring and evaluation frameworks, conducting qualitative and quantitative data collection and analysis, and reporting performance results against key performance indicators. Experience in statistical modeling/analysis is a plus.
  • Expertise and competence in project monitoring and evaluation, preferably related to international development work and in one or more of NDI’s program areas: e.g., civil society strengthening, democratic political institution strengthening, elections, women’s political empowerment, political inclusion of marginalized groups, etc.

REQUIRED SKILLS

  • Demonstrated competency in qualitative and quantitative research/data collection and data analysis/management, including the use and management of databases and related modeling and report preparation, and experience with database management, preferably with experience with MS Excel, MS Access, or other monitoring and evaluation platforms;
  • Demonstrated knowledge and understanding of monitoring and evaluation frameworks, including routine data collection, data quality assurance, and promoting data for decision making and interventions/learning;
  • Experience in designing and using evaluation tools and methods such as surveys, interviews, focus groups, and research from secondary sources;
  • Knowledge and expertise related to international donor monitoring, evaluation, and learning requirements to support program life cycles, ensure compliance, promote accountabilities, and support progress reporting;
  • Fluency in English, and excellent written and oral communication skills to present information and respond to questions. Language skills in Asian languages are a plus;
  • Problem-solving skills for identifying problems, drawing conclusions, determining options for resolution, and recommending next steps;
  • Strong interpersonal skills and cultural sensitivity to interact effectively and diplomatically with individuals at all levels of the organization, as well as externally-both domestically and internationally with NDI partners, funders and other stakeholders;
  • Capacity to work effectively both independently and as a member of a team, as well as to provide guidance to others;
  • Strong organizational skills with a high level of attention to detail;
  • Strong working knowledge of PC-based word processing and spreadsheet applications and experience with Google Apps (Gmail, Calendar, Google Drive, G+, etc.).

COMMENTS:

The application deadline is October 19. To apply, please e-mail a CV and cover letter to asiarecruitment@ndi.org.

Short-listed candidates will be contacted. No phone calls, please!

Applicants need to possess work authorization to work in Nepal.

NDI is an Equal Opportunity Employer and does not discriminate in employment opportunities or practices on the basis of race, color, religion, sex, national origin, age, disability, sexual orientation, gender identity, marital status, or any other characteristic protected by law.

ORGANIZATIONAL PROFILE

NNDSWO (1982) is a network based organization having its district chapters in 74 districts in Nepal. NNDSWO envisions an equitable and prosperous society free from all forms of discrimination, exploitation and poverty where human rights, social justice and dignity of all are equally respected. Gender equality, conflict transformation, youth empowerment, and advocacy on inclusive DRR are major crosscutting themes. The Executive Director is a leader of management team and under supervision of National President. S/he is responsible for developing policy, plan, programmes, project and budgets of the organization. The Executive Director makes decisions regarding day-to-day administrative functions as well as implementation of the programme activities under the constitution, guidance of policy, directives, decisions of the executive board of the organization.

  • Manage project cycle of all projects of organization and ensure proper design, implementation, monitoring and evaluation.

1. INTRODUCTION

About Forward Looking (FL)

Forward Looking, an NGO working for the person with disabilities (PWDs) to improve their quality of life through education support and economic empowerment. It has been implementing the Education Support Project (ESP) with grant support from Felm, Nepal.

The project aims to contribute to create an environment for the access to quality education for PWDs. Through the interventions of this project activities, ultimately the persons with disabilities have improved their dignified life, self-reliance and increases equal access to development benefits and services. Children with disabilities (CWDs) have increased their reach to quality education in an accessible educational institution. Persons with disabilities have improved their socio-economic status in conducive environment to enjoy their rights. Institutional and organizational capacity strengthened for policy, advocacy and disability inclusive development. The project has implemented in Kathmandu, Lalitpur, Dhading, Gorkha, Kaski, Baglung, Banke, Kailali and Surkhet districts.

2. Objectives

The evaluator is responsible for ensuring the safety, dignity, and voluntary participation of all individuals, with particular attention to vulnerable groups such as children, persons with disabilities, and marginalized populations.

Key principles include:

Informed Consent: All participants must give informed, voluntary consent. For minors or individuals with limited capacity, assent and guardian consent are required.

Forward Looking and Felm Nepal reserve the right to use and disseminate the findings for internal and external purposes. Unauthorized use by the evaluator may result in contractual or legal consequences.

description:
﻿﻿﻿Terms of Reference (ToR)

For Consultancy Services on

Soil Testing of Agricultural Land

Extended Notice

Background and Rationale:

Rural Development Centre (RDC) Nepal is a non-political and non-profitable organization established on May 2002 with its head office in Rautahat District, Madhesh Province, Nepal. Since then, RDC Nepal is heavily engaged in humanitarian assistance, community development, conservation of natural resources, and environmental protection mainly in the Terai region of Nepal through the dozens of humanitarian and long-term development projects reaching out to the children, adolescent, youth, women, landless, urban poor and people living with disabilities, HIV & AIDS patients, conflict and disaster survivors from the poor families of historically marginalized Dalits, Muslims, Madhesi and Indigenous communities and other underprivileged groups.

Throughout its journey, RDC Nepal has been recognized by the Government of Nepal, Donor Communities, UN Agencies, many International Relief and Development Agencies for its achievements in transforming the society, for its good governance, inclusive operating structure, result-oriented development interventions and humanitarian assistance, which RDC Nepal considers its greatest strength to take the lead in the social &development sector across the country.

For creating greater impact of its program, RDC Nepal has been working on advocacy & influencing on Climate Change, Disaster Management & another relevant sector. Since April 2025, RDC Nepal has been implementing Oxfam funded “Building Community Resilience to Climate Risks & Vulnerabilities (BCRC) Project” at Chandrapur and Gujara municipalities, Rautahat district, Madhesh Province, Nepal. While implementing the programs, RDC Nepal believes to build climate friendly environment through climate smart works in all the aspects. Climate change poses significant challenges to communities affecting various aspects of life including agriculture, health and livelihood and many more.

To support evidence-based nutrient management and improve vegetable productivity, soil testing is required across vegetable farms. This assignment aims to analyze soil samples from 95 farmers and 1 vermicompost sample to assess their physical and chemical properties.

Objective:

The main objective of this consultancy is to conduct laboratory testing of soil and vermicompost samples to determine key physical and chemical parameters, providing actionable data to inform soil fertility management practices.

Role or Scope of Work: 

The consultant/laboratory will be responsible for: 

  • Collecting the transported sample from the destination point delivered by the organization. 
  • Conducting laboratory analysis of each of the 95 soil samples and the one vermicompost sample for the parameters listed below: 

Parameters for 95 Soil samples: 

  1. Soil pH
  2. Soil Nitrogen (Total or Available, specify method)
  3. Available Phosphorus
  4. Available Potash (Potassium)
  5. Soil Texture (Sand, Silt, Clay percentage)
  6. Soil Organic Matter (OM)
  7. Electrical Conductivity (EC)
  8. Calcium (Ca)
  9. Magnesium (Mg)
  10. Sulphur (S)
  11. Boron (B)
  12. Zinc (Zn)
  13. Iron (Fe)
  14. Molybdenum (Mo)
  15. Manganese (Mn)

Parameters for 1 vermicompost sample: 

  1. pH
  2. Moisture 
  3. Organic Carbon (C)
  4. Total Nitrogen (N)
  5. Total Phosphorus (P₂O₅)
  6. Total Potas (K₂O)
  • Ensuring quality assurance during analysis. 
  • Preparing a comprehensive analytical report including raw data, interpretation, and recommendations. 

Deliverables:

1. A clear digital laboratory test reports for each soil sample and vermicompost sample. 

2. A summary report including: 

  • Overview of findings 
  • Methodologies applied for testing 
  • Interpretation of results with reference to standard fertility levels
  • Nutrient status classification (Low, Medium, High)
  • Recommendations for soil amendments and nutrient management 

Timeline:

The complete set of assignment should be completed by the end of October 2025. Lab reports and summary report should be shared by 28 October 2025. 

Responsibilities of RDC Nepal: 

  • Will collect the soil sample from the field. 
  • Transport the collected sample to the nearest areas of laboratory via local transport service. 
  • Review the lab reports and provide feedback incase required.

Consultant Qualification: 

  • Registered and accredited soil testing laboratory 
  • Proven experience in agriculture soil analysis
  • Trained personnel and modern analytical equipment
  • Capacity to deliver within stipulated time

﻿﻿﻿﻿Job Offer: School Program Coordinator at Akasha Academy

 

Akasha Academy is currently looking for a School Program Coordinator at the Headquarters site in Suntakhan, Gokarneshwor Municipality.


About Akasha Academy

Akasha Academy is creating pathways for the future of our planet, based on Universal Ethics.

The establishment of Akasha Academy in Nepal follows the vision of Tulku Khyungdor Rinpoche to offer a place for integrated education, rooted in the universal wisdom of original Buddhism. On that foundation, the main areas of work include education, health and environmental protection. A special focus is set on the empowerment of girls and women.

The Akasha Academy NGO is a non-governmental, non-profit organization registered in Nepal. The NGO's constitutional goal is to contribute to a positive and sustainable development through environmental protection, health promotion, education, and respect for human rights. The Akasha Academy NGO has been successfully carrying out projects since its foundation in 2012.

Akasha Academy is working closely together with its German sister organization Long Yang e.V.

More information: https://www.akasha-academy.org.np/

 

Development of Akasha Academy Headquarters

The Headquarters of Akasha Academy is located at the border of Shivapuri National Park in Suntakhan, Gokarneshwor Municipality. It is envisioned to serve as a flagship project for sustainable land use, planning, architecture, and infrastructure. The master planning of the land with sustainable architecture and infrastructure is currently in the making. Akasha Academy also supports local food systems and runs a model farm for regenerative, organic agriculture in Suntakhan, offering healthy locally grown food as well as training for the local community in these fields.

Akasha Education

In view of the current global and local developments, it has become increasingly clear that there is a need to support especially the younger generation in being able to meet today's challenges.

This is how the vision of Akasha Academy as a place for integrated education in the fields of health and environment came into being. The aim of Akasha Education is to create conditions for young people from diverse backgrounds to find their path in life and give them the necessary tools to face the current challenges globally and locally. Akasha Education programs in Nepa currently consist of different workshops and the Akasha Traineeship, a vocational training for women.

Akasha Environment

The vision of Akasha Academy also includes ecosystems restoration, reforestation, enhancing the local biodiversity, sustainable land use and regenerative, organic farming principles as well as training for the local community in these fields. Furthermore, we engage the community in clean-up campaigns, plantation activities and through awareness campaigns. We work with the local government, public schools, women’s groups and small-holder farmers to contribute to a positive development towards healthy people and ecosystems in the area.

A new project, starting from November will combine education and environment and focus on an awareness program on environmental and climate change education for 16 public schools in Gokarneshwor Municipality.

 

Role of the position

The role of the School Program Coordinator will focus mainly on the coordination of workshops and activities in collaboration with all 16 public schools of Gokarneshwor Municipality as well as the coordination of curriculum and content development. For the position, daily presence at the premises in Suntakhan (Gokarneshwor) will be required. The ideal candidate would be ready to relocate or stay nearby during the working week.  

 

Contract period

Initially 1 year, with the possibility of extension; long-term engagement envisioned

 

Tasks and responsibilities:

·       Coordination of various activities and regular events with all 16 schools of Gokarneshwor Municipality

·       Preparing and organizing the development of a curriculum for the school program related to environmental protection and climate change adaptation in line with the organization’s education approach

·       Coordination and communication with different government stakeholders, school management committees, and other working partners of Akasha Academy

·       Supervision and coordination of assistant trainers of the school program

·       Monitoring and reporting on progress related to the project, ensuring to keep agreed upon timelines,

·       Represent the organization at relevant events, support in expanding the network to relevant public and private stakeholders

·       Further develop the program according to the larger vision of the organization, support in proposal development

·       Regular travel and visits to all 16 public schools of the municipality

 

Required skills and experience:

Bachelor's, preferably Master’s Degree or Diploma in relevant discipline, i.e. education, social work, project management, environmental sciences, etc.

At least 3 years work experience in the education and/or development sector, in one or more of the following areas: education, environmental protection and awareness, climate change adaptation, youth empowerment, or similar

Proven experience in leadership, project management and coordination,

proven experience in working with children and youth 

sound knowledge on child safeguarding 

excellent communication and presentation skills,

be courageous, curios and innovative

the capability to manage schedules of multiple topics and to manage unexpected situations calmly and in a flexible way,

solid command of Nepali and English languages, both written and verbal,

the ability to work within a team of different social and cultural backgrounds,

reliability and loyalty,

the aspiration to contribute to a positive change in local communities and beyond,

a strong identification and commitment towards the overall project aim and the work of Akasha Academy NGO,

solid command of MS Office package (especially Powerpoint, Word, Excel)

driver’s license (Two wheeler)

 

Ideally, you have

-          practical leadership experience in similar setting

-          strong network and advocacy skills

-          experience in education and coordination with schools, government and community stakeholders

 

Candidates interested in working with Akasha Academy NGO are requested to send their complete application, including CV, motivation letter and expected salary in English language, to hr(at)akasha-academy.org until 23.10.2025. Applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis and the advertisement might be closed prior to the deadline, if suitable candidates apply.

 

In case of questions, do not hesitate to contact us. We are looking forward to hearing from you.

लि–बर्डद्वारा सञ्चालित The Green Evolution: Pathways to transforming food systems परियोजनाका लागि निम्न सामग्रीहरू खरिद गर्नुपर्ने भएकोले इच्छुक तथा योग्य विक्रेतालाई यो सूचना प्रकाशित भएको मितिले १४ (चौध) दिन भित्र ली–बर्ड प्रधान कार्यालय, पोखरा–१२, कास्की अथवा ली–बर्ड कार्यक्रम समन्वय कार्यालय, सानेपा, ललितपुरमा गोप्य शिलबन्दी बोलपत्र पेश गर्नको लागि आह्वान गरिन्छ ।

पेश भएका बोलपत्र स्वीकृत गर्ने वा नगर्ने अन्तिम निर्णय गर्ने अधिकार ली–बर्डमा सुनिश्चित रहने छ । शिलबन्दी बोलपत्र संस्थाको केन्द्रीय कार्यालय, पोखरा अथवा कार्यक्रम समन्वय कार्यालय, सानेपामा मिति २०८२ कार्तिक ०२ गते बेलुका ५:०० बजेभित्र दर्ता गराउनु पर्नेछ । बोलपत्र आवेदन फाराम (प्राविधिक फारम र वित्तिय फारम) मा संलग्न विवरणहरू तथा तिनमा उल्लेखित शर्तहरूलाई यसै सूचनाको अभिन्न अङ्ग मानी अनिवार्य रुपमा पूरा गर्नुपर्नेछ । प्राविधिक फारम र वित्तिय फारम मिति २०८२ असोज १९ गतेबाट २०८२ असोज ३१ गते विहान ९ बजे देखि बेलुका ५ बजेसम्म (शनिबार र आईतबार अफिस बन्द रहनेछ) ली–बर्डको केन्द्रीय कार्यालय, पोखरा तथा ली–बर्डको कार्यक्रम समन्वय कार्यालय, सानेपाबाट प्राप्त गर्न सकिनेछ ।

नोटः यो खरिद प्रक्रियालाई कुनै पनि चरणमा संशोधन, स्थगित अथवा रद्द गर्ने अधिकार ली–बर्डमा सुनिश्चित रहनेछ र बोलपत्र तयार पार्ने तथा पेश गर्ने क्रममा लाग्ने सम्पूर्ण खर्च सम्बन्धित बिक्रेताले स्वयं व्यहोर्नु पर्नेछ ।

description:
﻿Background:

NEEDS Nepal, a Kanchanpur-based NGO established in 1999, has been actively involved in enhancing community resilience to natural disasters. Nepal is recognized as highly vulnerable to climate-induced disasters like floods, landslides, and droughts, urgently needs a robust multi-hazard early warning system to support anticipatory action. To address this, a Decision Support System (DSS) will enhance the existing BIPAD Portal by integrating official forecasts, hazard models, and Earth Observation data (e.g., IMERG, MODIS, Sentinel), enabling real-time monitoring and impact forecasting across key sectors. This system will deliver localized, time-sensitive alerts to guide early action and humanitarian response, strengthening disaster preparedness and resilience nationwide.

name: Rural Women's Development and Unity Centre (RUWDUC)
job-title: Call for Application: Fellowship Grant Support for Three Students
description:
﻿Rural Women's Development and Unity Centre (RUWDUC)

Sankhamul, Kathmandu Phone number 01-4533662, P.O Box # 13205

TRANSBOUNDARY RIVERS OF SOUTH ASIA (TROSA: T2:3R)

Call for Application: Fellowship Grant Support for Three Students

Details/requirements :

Date of Publication: 7th October, 2025

Rural Women Development and Unity Centre (RUWDUC) is a non-profit, non-governmental organization that has been actively engaged in the social development sector since 1995. Since its establishment, RUWDUC has been a strong advocate for the rights and empowerment of women, children, and youth. The organization strives to promote human well-being and ensure equality for all by enhancing access to education, healthcare, justice, and a violence-free society.

In line with its vision and mission, RUWDUC, in collaboration with Oxfam in Nepal, has been implementing the Transboundary Rivers of South Asia (TROSA) program in Dadeldhura District. The first phase of TROSA concluded in March 2022, while TROSA Phase II has been underway since June 2023 and will continue until March 2026.

RUWDUC is now seeking three student fellows under its fellowship grant program to support the following activities:

2. Research Grant Opportunity

RUWDUC invites three Bachelor's Degree holder (masters preferred) to apply for a youth fellowship grant of NPR 100,000 (including tax). Youth Fellow initiatives are expected to lay foundations for meaningful transformation or solution to the challenges faced by grassroots communities associated with the Mahakali Basin. It could be a range of things, starting from research, documentation of indigenous knowledge revival, on-ground actions and anything innovative of its kind addresses water governance challenges in the wider sense. These initiatives are expected to be done in partnership with the communities they serve and also bring about growth to the youth leading these initiatives and add value to their journey as leaders.

3. Priorities Area of Research

Proposals must be aligned with one of the following priorities. One student will be selected for one particular topic.

  • Transboundary Cooperation Through Shared Water Governance
  • Climate resilience livelihoods in Mahkali Basin
  • Citizen Science in Water Quality Monitoring of the Mahakali River: Scope, Practices, and Sustainability

4. Eligibility Criteria for Applicants:

The Youth Fellow Initiative for Mahakali basin is open to young water leaders aged 29 years or below residing within any of the Mahakali basin. Eligible participants can apply either as individuals or as part of a group. Proposals are welcome from independent applicants as well as those affiliated with organizations. This initiative encourages innovative ideas and collaborative efforts to address water-related challenges in the region. Women and youth from indigenous or marginalised river dependent communities are strongly encouraged to apply.

5. Application Process

Interested applicants are invited to submit their proposal and CV to the official email address of RUWDUC ruwducvacancy@gmail.com. The submitted information will be used as the basis for the shortlisting process. Applicants are requested to select one relevant topic for their research and prepare their proposal accordingly.

6. Evaluation Process

The evaluation process will prioritize initiatives that are inclusive, intersectional, innovative, and effectively address water-related challenges within the Mahakali basin. All eligible applications will undergo a thorough review by a dedicated committee comprising experts on water issues in Mahakali basin. This committee will evaluate submissions against predefined criteria and determine grant allocation. Shortlisted candidates will proceed to the next phase, where they will receive orientation to meet the objective of their study and be invited to submit a full comprehensive proposal detailing their initiative. Final selection will be based on the strength of these proposals, and support will be provided accordingly.

7. Evaluation Criteria

I. Relevance: The proposed initiative must align with the pressing needs of the communities dependent on the Mahakali River basin for transboundary cooperation, climate resilience livelihoods, citizen science in its scope, and survival. Initiatives that are well studies/documents the power relations, vulnerabilities, rights, justice, and opportunities in the context of their river basins will be prioritized.

II. Potential Impact: The initiative/research should advocate for the equitable use of water resources, addressing social and environmental equity challenges, and fostering inclusive and resilient communities.

III. Innovation, Creativity and Capacity: Novel and effective strategies, especially for engaging women, youth, and Indigenous peoples, addressing policy gaps, participation and influencing stakeholders.

IV. Sustainability and Scalability: The initiative needs to address sustainability and beyond as the result of study/research or influencing policy and advocacy to ensure long-term impact.

8. Reporting Requirements

The YF will receive an orientation on the Mahakali basin, TROSA’s working areas, and mutual expectations. This will be followed by two follow-up meetings to track progress and provide necessary support. The final report is due by 26 January 2026.

9. Timeline of the Initiative

10. Grant Utilization

The maximum support is worth NPR One Lakh per YF. The payment will be done in two installments: 40% upon awarding the Youth Fellowship and 60% upon submission and approval of the final report. Shortlisted candidates are expected to share a detailed support breakdown with their overall initiative plan.

name: Dolphin Conservation Center
job-title: Terms of Reference For Preparation of Sustainable Riverbed Sand, Stone and Gravel Mining Protocol
description:
﻿Terms of Reference

For

Preparation of Sustainable Riverbed Sand, Stone and Gravel Mining Protocol

1. Background:

The Lower Karnali Watershed covers 747 km2 in Nepal’s Terai Arc Landscape. Rich in aquatic biodiversity, it harbors 136 fish species and provides ecosystem services for local communities. The watershed provides a rich mosaic of habitats that includes rivers, riverine forests, floodplain grasslands and oxbow lakes which is suitable for a large number of fish species and provides habitat for many IUCN Red List species such as Gharial Crocodile (critically endangered), Mugger Crocodile (vulnerable), Gangetic River Dolphin (endangered) and Smooth-Coated Otter (vulnerable). Considering its significance, the Government of Nepal prioritized the western channel of Karnali River as an ecological corridor and the eastern channel is included in Bardia National Park buffer zone

Otter species are an ecological indicator of healthy aquatic ecosystems and protected by the amended Aquatic Animal Protection Act 2002 of the Government of Nepal. However, declining fish diversity and abundance due to overfishing and habitat disturbance caused by intensive river aggregates extraction threaten the health of the river ecosystem and declining smooth-coated otter populations. Limited research on their distribution hampers development of an effective national otter conservation strategy.

Illegal and unsustainable fishing is prevalent in western channels of Karnali River due to interlinked drivers- limited capacity to enforce fisheries regulations and insufficient fisheries management procedures. Unregulated riverbed sand, stone and gravel mining has rapidly increased in the western belt of the Karnali. Local governments have limited capacity to ensure sustainable extraction and contractors extract aggregates without following environmental management plans required by Initial Environmental Examination (IEE) reports. Weak compliance and monitoring mechanisms from local governments allow degradation of river systems and otter habitat, destroying vegetation and fish spawning sites which has caused a sharp decline in fish diversity and abundance, threatening the traditional livelihoods and food security of indigenous and marginalized Sonaha and Tharu communities.  In these regards, DCC has been strengthening the capacity of representatives from local governments, government line agencies and law enforcement agencies to enhance the conservation of river ecosystem benefiting both freshwater species and dependent local communities. This task is to support local governments especially Bhajani Municipality, Rajapur Municipality and Joshipur Rural Municipality in preparing their Sustainable Riverbed Sand, Stone and Gravel Mining Protocols.

2. Objective:

The primary objectives of the research are:

  • To develop a protocol for sustainable management of riverbed sand, stone and gravel mining maintaining socio-ecological balance
  • Develop monitoring mechanisms to assess the impact of extraction activities and ensure compliance with environmental regulation and promote sustainable practice among stakeholders
  • Prepare a standard for extraction, collection and transportation of the riverbed sand, stone and gravel  

3. Methodology:

Literature review:

The review of relevant scientific articles, reports, and policies concerning the regulation of illegal extraction of river products from the Karnali River, particularly in otter and aquatic animal hotspot areas, shall be conducted in collaboration with the community. 

Consultation/Interaction/Meetings:

Series of interactive programs, including workshops and meetings, shall be conducted with the community, relevant government and non-government organizations, experts, academia, the community river stretch management groups, forestry user groups, the Division Forest Office, and local communities, either together or separately, as needed for effective management of the sand, stone and gravel mining from the Karnali River in otter habitat areas. 

Field investigation:

Field visits shall be conducted by an interdisciplinary team comprising, but not limited to, an ecologist, sociologist, hydrologist, and watershed expert. The team will need to gather all relevant facts, figures, and information from the field, either through scientific studies or various levels of meetings, as previously described.

Draft sharing:

The team shall share the draft protocols with the local government representatives, including Environmental Focal Points and members of relevant Municipal Environmental Committees, community river stretch management groups, community forest user groups, water users groups, relevant experts, local CSOs and indigenous peoples and local communities  for their constructive engagement in the process and to incorporate their voices in the protocols The consultant team shall work closely with the river adjoining local governments while preparing the Protocol. 

Final sharing meeting:

The final draft will be shared with experts and relevant stakeholders at the local level government. Comments, suggestions, and feedback received shall be incorporated into the final protocol. The final protocols shall be submitted to the respective local government and receive approval and endorsement accordingly.

4. Time Frame and Schedule:

A maximum of 3 months is estimated for this work considering the required field visits.

S.N.Scope of WorkDue Date
1.Literature review17th Oct -30th Oct 2025
2.Stakeholders’ meetings/consultation workshops and sharing workshop1st Nov– 21st Nov 2025
3.Field visit and consultations in field7th Nov-28th Nov,2025
4.Draft protocol presentation18th Nov -1st Dec 2025
5.Final Submission and sharing workshop of the protocol7th Dec -19th Dec, 2025

5. Deliverables

  • Three Protocols for sustainable riverbed sand, stone and gravel mining and endorsement from the respective local governments.
  • Digital photographs of meetings/workshops. 
  • Financial report with supporting invoices.

6. Team Composition and Qualification

The team should comprise ecologist, sociologist, hydrologist and geology expert.

1. Team Leader:

Qualification and competency of Team Leader

  • Masters’ Degree in Environment Science/ Management, Aquatic Biodiversity, River Geomorphology, Hydrogeology, Forestry, Natural Resources Management or related discipline with at least 10 years of experience in sustainable riverbed sand, stone and gravel mining and environmental assessment

2. Geologist with experience analyzing the geological aspects of riverbed materials:

Qualification of Geologist:

  • Masters degree in geology or geotechnical engineering
  • At least 5 years of experience in IEE/EIA Preparation of river sediment.

3. Sociologist/Gender and Social Inclusion expert

Qualification and competency of Sociologist

  • Master’s Degree in Sociology/Gender/economics/development studies   related discipline
  • At least 5 years of working experience in gender and social inclusion in natural resources management sector, including IEE/EIA preparation for sandstone and gravel mining 
  • Should have knowledge on environment and social safeguard

4. Hydrologist with hydrological impacts of river aggregates extraction on river flow, sediment transport, and water quality.

Qualification of a Hydrologist:

  • At least bachelor’s degree in civil engineering/ Hydrology/ Water Resources Management
  • At least 2 years of experience in hydrology, water resource management and river dynamics

7. Budget

Interested VAT registered individuals/organizations should submit a Technical and financial proposal that includes a detailed breakdown of total activities and budget: Expert fee, meeting cost, travel cost, communication costs and other costs, if any. (including 13% VAT)

8. Consultant Selection Process:

Consultants will be selected based on technical and financial proposals following DCC Nepal's standard procedure for procurement of consultancy services.

9. Proposal Submission Details

Interested VAT registered individuals /organizations are requested to submit technical and financial proposals via email by 17th October 2025.

10. Mode of Payment

The payment will be made as per Dolphin Conservation Center's norms and upon submissions of satisfactory deliverables. Note that payments are subject to tax deduction as per prevailing government rules.

Organization Registration, and latest renewal - applicable to NGO

name: WWF Nepal
job-title: Call for proposals: Cost-Benefit Analysis of Nature-Based Solutions in the Lower Narayani River Basin
description:
﻿WWF Nepal seeks consultancy services to conduct a Cost-Benefit Analysis (CBA) of nature-based solutions (NbS) implemented in the Khageri and Gindri watersheds of the Lower Narayani River Basin. The analysis will assess the ecological, social, and economic performance of interventions like wetland restoration, soil conservation, and diversified resilient livelihoods. The consultancy will compare NbS with conventional grey infrastructure alternatives and produce a detailed analytical report, including a manuscript for submission to a peer-reviewed journal.

description:
﻿निड्स नेपाल

कञ्चनपुर

शिलबन्दी बोलपत्र आह्वानको सूचना

प्रथम पटक प्रकाशित मिति २०८२/०६/१२

OXFAM नेपाल तथा KOICA को सहयोग र राष्ट्रिय वातावरण तथा सम विकास समाज नेपालद्वारा यस कञ्चनपुर जिल्लामा संचालित “Empowering Her: Advancing Women’s Economic and Poltical Leadrership For Climate Resilient Communities Project” अन्तर्गत विभिन्न जलवायु मैत्री कृषि जन्य सामाग्री र उपकरणहरू खरिद गर्नु पर्ने भएकोले ईच्छुक आपुर्तीकर्ता/विक्रेताहररूबाट रीतपुर्वक शिलवन्दी बोलपत्र आह्वाान गरिन्छ ।

क्र.सं.बोलपत्र नं.विवरणथप जानकारी
१1076-001-2025/26कृषि जन्य सामाग्री र उपकरणहरूतल दिईएको फोन नम्बर वा ई–मेलमा सम्पर्क गरी जानकारी लिन सकिनेछ ।

१. सम्बन्धीत विषयको ईजाजत प्राप्त आपुर्तीकर्ता/विक्रेताले यस संस्थाको केन्द्रिय कार्यालय भिमदत्त–१८, कञ्चनपुरमा सम्पर्क गरी माग गर्नु पर्नेछ अथवा तलका लिंक बाट बोलपत्रका कागजातहरू डाउनलोड गर्न सकिन्छ ।

२. यो सूचना प्रकाशित भएको मितिले ३० दिन भित्र रितपूर्वक भरिे बोलपत्र फारामको प्रत्येक पानामा सम्बन्धीत आपूर्तिकर्ता वा कम्पनीको आधिकारिक हस्ताक्षर र छाप अनिवार्य रुपमा लगाई लाहा छापबाट शिलबन्दी गरी प्राबिधिक र आर्थिक प्रस्तावना छुट्टाछुट्टै खाममा संस्थाको केन्द्रिय कार्यालय भिमदत्त–१८, कञ्चनपुरमा आपुर्तिकर्ताको स्वंम भौतिक उपस्थिति वा आधिकारिक प्रतिनिधिको भौतिक उपस्थितिमा हार्डकपी मिति २०८२/०७/१० गते बेलुकी ४ बजे भित्र अथवा ई–मेल मार्फत बुझाउन सकिनेछ । बोलपत्र बुझाउने प्रकृया बारे प्राविधिक प्रस्तावनामा विस्तृत रुपमा उल्लेख गरिएको छ ।

३. बोलपत्र फारम प्राप्त गर्ने अन्तिम मिति २०८२/०६/३० गते रहने छ भने र त्यस पछि बोलपत्र बितरण गरिने छैन । वोलपत्रका सर्तहरू स्पष्ट गर्नकालागि ईच्छुक आपुर्तीकर्ता वा विक्रेता सगं पुर्व वोलपत्र वैठक मिति २०८२ कार्तिक २ गते दिउसो १२ वजेवाट अनलाईन र भौतिक उपस्थिति मार्फत आयोजना गरिने छ । बोलपत्र पेश गर्ने अन्तिम दिन सार्वजनिक बिदा परेको खण्डमा सो दिनको भोली पल्ट शिलबन्दी बोलपत्र फारम बुझाउने, बुझिलिने काम हुनेछ । बोलपत्र फारम मिति २०८२/०७/ १४ गते दिउँसो ११ बजे देखि सम्पुर्ण आपूर्तिकर्ताको भौतिक उपस्तिथिमा यस संस्थाको केन्द्रिय कार्यालय भिमदत्त–१८, कञ्चनपुरमा खोलिने छ ।

४. बोलपत्र, पूर्ण वा आंशिक रूपमा कुनै कारण जनाई वा नजनाई स्वीकृत गर्ने वा नगर्ने वा सूचना नै रद्ध गर्ने सम्पूर्ण अधिकार यस निड्स नेपाल कञ्चनपुरको खरिद समितिमा निहित रहने छ ।

५. रितपूर्वक नभरी बोलपत्र पेश भएको वा नपुगेको वा म्याद भित्र प्राप्त हुन नआएको बोलपत्र उपर कुनै पनि कारवाही गरिने छैन । उक्त बोलपत्रहरुलाई स्वतः रद्द भएको मानिनेछ ।

६. यस सूचनामा उल्लेख गरिएका शर्तहरू यसै सूचना बमोजिम र अन्य आवश्यक कुराहरूको हकमा यसै संस्थाको बन्दोबस्ती तथा खरिद नियमावली २०८० बमोजिम हुनेछ ।

name: Pro Public
description:
﻿﻿﻿﻿﻿Vacancy Announcement

Strengthening Civil Society for Inclusive Democracy and Human Rights in Nepal and the Philippines (SAMA-SAMA) is a 3-year development project managed by the Centre for International Studies and Cooperation (CECI), with the funding support from Global Affairs Canada (GAC). Forum for Protection of Public Interest (Pro Public), established in 1991, a national-level non-governmental organization working in the areas of democracy, good governance, inclusion, gender equality, social justice, and civic engagement, is the project thematic partner for the implementation of this project. This Project aims to strengthen civil society in Nepal to reinforce civic engagement and democratic participation among women and marginalized groups (WMGs).

To fulfill the following position of the project, Pro Public is seeking qualified and motivated Nepali citizens.

Position: Admin & Finance Officer – 1

Project: Strengthening Civil Society for Inclusive democracy and Human Rights (SAMA-SAMA) 

Location: Kathmandu, Nepal

Reports To: Project Manager

Contract Type: Project-based, full-time

Duration: Five months, renewable based on performance and project needs (November 1, 2025 start)

Position Overview:

The Admin & Finance Officer is responsible for the project's overall financial management, administration, and logistical support. S/he ensures financial systems and procedures comply with donor, government, and organizational guidelines. The Admin &Finance Officer also provides critical administrative support for smooth project operations. 

Duties and Responsibilities:

  • Prepare and manage the project budget in close coordination with the Governance and Inclusion Advisor, Project Manager, and other project team of the SAMA-SAMA Project.
  • Monitor financial transactions to ensure accuracy, integrity, and compliance with donor requirements.
  • Process payments, maintain petty cash, and manage bank transactions and reconciliations.
  • Prepare monthly, quarterly, and annual financial reports for internal and external stakeholders.
  • Coordinate and support external and internal audits, ensuring proper documentation and follow-up on audit findings.
  • Lead procurement processes in accordance with organizational and donor procurement policies.
  • Maintain inventory and asset records, ensuring safe and proper utilization.
  • Support financial arrangements for training, workshops, and events held at national and provincial levels.
  • Handle correspondence, documentation, and filing of administrative and financial records.
  • Support scheduling and coordination of meetings, trainings, and travels.
  • Ensure smooth day-to-day administrative operations, including office supply management and vendor communications.
  • Perform other duties as assigned or as required to support the organization’s needs.

Qualifications and Experience:

  • At least a Bachelor's degree in Business Administration with specialization in Finance, and a minimum of three years of relevant experience.
  • Strong commitment and capability to support day-to-day administrative and financial operations.
  • Proven skills in drafting official correspondence, taking meeting minutes, maintaining organized documentation, and facilitating internal and external communications.
  • Proficient in accounting software (e.g., FAMAS, Tally, QuickBooks) and MS Office Suite.
  • Experience preparing budgets and developing financial proposals for new project initiatives and expansion.
  • Ability to work effectively in a diverse team environment, manages multiple tasks under pressure, and adapt to shifting priorities.
  • Good command of both Nepali and English, in speaking and writing.
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office (Word, Excel, PowerPoint), email and internet tools, Google Drive, and Nepali typing (Preeti or Unicode).
  • Possession of a valid motorbike driving license will be an added advantage.

Reporting and Supervision:

The Admin and Finance Officer will report to the Project Manager and will coordinate closely with overall project team

Remuneration and Benefits:

The monthly remuneration for the Admin and Finance Officer is NPR 40,000.00 with an additional 30% in benefits.

description:
﻿REQUEST FOR PROPOSALS: Final Project Evaluation of NP07 Building Climate Resilience and Reintegrating Economically Displaced Workers through Climate Smart Agriculture in the Terai Flood Plain, Nepal

Global Green Growth Institute Nepal Program

Based in Seoul, The Global Green Growth Institute (GGGI) is an intergovernmental organization founded to support and promote a model of economic growth known as "green growth", which targets key aspects of economic performance such as poverty reduction, job creation, social inclusion, and environmental sustainability. GGGI works with countries around the world, building their capacity and working collaboratively on green growth policies that can impact the lives of millions. The organization partners with countries, multilateral institutions, government bodies, and private sectors to help build economies that grow strongly and are more efficient and sustainable in the use of natural resources, less carbon intensive, and more resilient to climate change.

Details/requirements:

Final Project Evaluation of NP07 Building Climate Resilience and Reintegrating Economically Displaced Workers through Climate Smart Agriculture in the Terai Flood Plain, Nepal

Date documents can be Submitted until: 27 October 2025 16:00 Korean Standard Time.

Title: Final Project Evaluation of NP07 Building Climate Resilience and Reintegrating Economically Displaced Workers through Climate Smart Agriculture in the Terai Flood Plain, Nepal

Procurement No.: 100013741

Process: RFP

Description:

The Global Green Growth Institute (GGGI) is inviting eligible firms/entities to submit their proposals for the following scope of work under the project NP07 Building Climate Resilience and Reintegrating Economically Displaced Workers through Climate Smart Agriculture in the Terai Flood Plain, Nepal.

PROJECT BACKGROUND:

GGGI Nepal has been implementing the project “Building Climate Resilience and Reintegrating Economically Displaced Workers through Climate Smart Agriculture (CSA) in the Terai Flood Plain” in 10 selected municipalities of Dhanusha and Mahottari districts in Madhesh Province from June 2022 to December 2025.

The project aims to support widespread adoption of climate-smart agriculture to reduce vulnerability and improve food and job security, especially for women, youth and returned migrant workers through 3 objectives. To achieve one of the objectives to strengthen resilient agriculture planning and implementation, GGGI has identified the need to equip farmers with climate-resilient technology relevant to agriculture value chain production (Output 1.2). Output 1.2 will support municipalities in developing a Climate Smart Agriculture (CSA) plan, ensure the CSA plan is adopted by municipalities, and support the implementation of CSA measures and public work to build resilience for farming communities.

Target Beneficiaries: The direct beneficiaries are expected to be 350 (full time public labors job creation) from 10 municipalities and the number of indirect beneficiaries (residents benefiting from the project) is 4,13,358.

Geographic Target: The project is being implemented in Kamala, Sabaila, Mithila Bihari, Janaknandini and Mukhiyapatti Musaharniya municipalities of Dhanusha district and Matihani, Mahottari, Sonama, Balwa and Bhangaha municipalities of Mahottari district.

The purpose of this Final Project Evaluation of NP07 (CSA) is to assess the results and effectiveness of the project, the sustainability of the project, identify lessons learned, and examine the real changes on the project’s primary target groups - women and youth. 

EVALUATION OBJECTIVE:

The purpose of this evaluation is to assess the results and effectiveness of the project, the sustainability of the project, identify lessons learned, and examine the real changes on the project’s primary target groups - women and youth. The evaluation will aim to:

  • Review the progress in achieving the Project’s results, tracing the factors that have led to the current situation, both positive and limitations.
  • Distill lessons learned from the Project’s implementation, and the circumstances under which they are transferable to other contexts; and
  • Generate evidence-based recommendations that can inform the design of similar future projects, and/or review the sustainability of the project.

For further details on the Scope of Work, please refer to the Terms of Reference available under the published Document Set.

IMPORTANT TIMELINES:

The tender submission deadline is 27 October 2025, 16:00 pm KST (Korean Standard Time) / 7:00 am GMT.

Note: If any bidder has any request for clarification on the TOR or any part of the tender documents, GGGI will be happy to clarify if the request is received on or before 7 days before the deadline (namely: if the tender submission deadline is 16:00 15 April KST, then the due date for submission of request for clarification is 16:00 8 April KST).

Interested parties will be required to register their details on the GGGI e-Green Procurement Portal (Global Green Growth Institute (GGGI) e-Green Procurement Portal - Login).

HOW TO OBTAIN THE DOCUMENTS:

Documents can be accessed via the e-Green Procurement Portal by selecting ‘View Details on the relevant notice and then clicking the ‘Tender Application’ button. If you are a new supplier, you will be required to register your details. If you have an existing account, you will need to login to the portal. Please refer to the guidance documents under the `Supplier Guidance` area of the portal for further information.

ONLINE TENDER MANAGEMENT:

Once in the Tender Management Area for the tender, there are five possible tabs: Tender’, `Tender Documents, Correspondence’, Clarifications’ and ‘History’. Select the 2nd tab (`Tender Documents`) where you will find useful information regarding the RFP. Scroll down to the heading ‘Tender Documents Received’ where you will be able to view / download the documents.

OPTING IN & OPTING OUT:

Please note that you may be required to ‘Opt In’ before you can start populating your response. The ‘Opt Out’ functionality will also be available throughout the duration of the tender process. Opting out will give you the option of declaring you no longer want to receive any further communication in relation to this tender along with the opportunity of providing comments and feedback for this decision. You can choose to ‘Opt In’ at any time during the tender process if you initially decided to ‘Opt Out’.

SUBMITTING YOUR RESPONSE VIA THE PORTAL:

Please note that you may be required to ‘Opt In’ to be able to submit a response through the portal. Tenderers will be required to upload any mandatory Placeholders (i.e. specified documents) within the `Tender Documents` tab. The ability to attach additional documents may also be available. Your proposal will not be submitted until you click `Submit Return`, located towards the bottom of the screen. On clicking `Submit Return`, you will receive a receipt confirming that your proposal has been submitted to GGGI.

Please read Instructions on How to submit the Proposal.

NOTIFICATION EMAILS:

To ensure you receive email alerts and notifications from our system, please add the email domain `@in-tendorganiser.co.uk` to your Safe Senders list.

Adara Development is committed to improving health, education, and community resilience outcomes in Nepal. We are seeking to recruit a passionate and skilled Research, Monitoring, Evaluation and Learning (RMEL) Officer to join our team in Nepal. Applications are invited from competent and qualified Nepali citizens. Please submit your CV, cover letter and details for 2 referees with your application.

The Research, Monitoring, Evaluation, and Learning Officer (RMELO) plays a key role in implementing Adara’s RMEL strategic plan in Nepal. Working closely with the RMEL Manager, the global RMEL team, and the broader Nepal team, the RMELO strengthens evidence-based decision-making across Adara’s programmes in health, education, community resilience, child protection, and youth development.

The RMELO also supports the development of RMEL tools, contributes to analysis and reporting, prepares case studies and knowledge products, and facilitates feedback loops with teams and stakeholders.
